subject: HelixData replacement — pricing alignment and infra compatibility
messages:
From: Caroline Hayes <caroline.hayes@helixdata.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluating replacement — pricing & runtime questions

Jonas,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, HelixData is kicking off a formal evaluation to replace our current inference vendor. Two quick asks so we can brief procurement:

- Can Redwood match the blended effective price we currently pay (we'll share the invoice line items)? We're looking for a 12–18 month migration with a pilot, and any upfront credits would help.
- We need a compatibility summary: runtime-level differences we should expect (KV cache persistency, prompt-size limits, quantization artifacts). We run spikey workloads with bursts to 600 rps across 3 regions.

Attached is our compatibility spreadsheet (platform-compatibility-matrix.xlsx) that lists current hooks & infra constraints.

Procurement will want an initial commercial framework and a high-level mutual action plan (MAP) so they can assess timeline risk. Can you get something over by EOD next Monday?

—Caroline Hayes
Head of ML Engineering, HelixData
[Attachment: platform-compatibility-matrix.xlsx]
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Caroline Hayes <caroline.hayes@helixdata.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 17:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Evaluating replacement — pricing & runtime questions

Caroline —

Appreciate the detailed matrix. High level answer up front: we can present a commercial that narrows to parity on per-token economics for your steady state, plus a staged credit that offsets migration risk (pilot credits + one-time migration credit). A few structural notes:

- Pricing anchors we typically offer: 6–12 month pilot credit (covering inference compute + egress), then a 12–24 month committed tier with blended unit price that improves with commit size.
- Migration credit sizing: we have a standard 3-month migration bucket (can flex to 6mo for larger deals) to cover parallel run costs, engineering handoff, and egress.
- Technical guardrails: we will guarantee feature parity for streaming & function-calling semantics; for KV-cache persistency we recommend our KV warm-start pattern (laura to detail below).

We need two things from you to finalize numbers: recent monthly token volumes (3-month view) and the subset of endpoints you expect to pilot (embedding vs. generation vs. chat). If procurement wants a formal term sheet I can send a draft — including canary / rollback language and a proposed SLA uplift during migration.

Proposed next steps:
1) Laura to follow up with a short note on runtime compatibility and pilot sizing.
2) We’ll draft a high-level MAP and commercial term sheet (Jonas).
3) Schedule technical pilot kick-off: target week of Jun 21.

I’ll attach a short-run term sheet and a pilot runbook in the next message.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-term-sheet-helixdata.pdf]
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Caroline Hayes <caroline.hayes@helixdata.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Evaluating replacement — pricing & runtime questions

Caroline — quick technical note from the infra side (longer runbook attached).

- KV cache: our recommended approach is a warm-start snapshot at pilot handoff (we persist the last epoch's KV shards to object storage and restore on first run). This avoids cold-start token spikes; expect a ~1–2s warming window for new pods.
- Quantization: we support INT8/4-bit paths. For your NLU models we expect negligible semantic drift in INT8; we can run a short A/B on 1K prompts to measure delta.
- Throughput: continuous batching + adaptive shard assignment should handle 600 rps bursts; we recommend an initial 4-GPU pilot pool (NVIDIA H100-equivalent) for the pilot.
- Data handling: logs and traces can be streamed to your SIEM; we support S3-compatible export for KV snapshots.

Attached: redwood-pilot-runbook.pdf (includes required IAM roles, network ACLs, and suggested observability traces).

Happy to hop on a call to walk through the runbook details.

—Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-pilot-runbook.pdf]
From: Caroline Hayes <caroline.hayes@helixdata.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@helixdata.com
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluating replacement — pricing & runtime questions

Thanks Jonas & Laura — useful detail. A couple of items procurement flagged as blockers before they let us proceed to a committed evaluation:

- We need a clear SLA uplift during the pilot window (99.5% p99 target or a credit alternative).
- Liability & indemnity: our legal team wants standard carveouts for data residency during the migration.
- Contract cadence: procurement prefers a 12-month committed term post-pilot; they asked whether Redwood will allow quarterly usage true-ups during the first year.

If you can put together a short commercial + MAP addressing those three bullets, procurement will greenlight the pilot. Also please include a named technical contact for the migration week.

—Caroline
(On behalf of HelixData procurement)
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Caroline Hayes <caroline.hayes@helixdata.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 17:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Evaluating replacement — pricing & runtime questions

Caroline — attaching the short commercial and MAP; summarized here so procurement can triage quickly.

Summary (high level):
- Pilot: 6-week pilot, 4-H100-equivalent GPUs, pilot credit covers 100% of compute for pilot up to 1.2M tokens and 50% egress.
- Migration credit: one-time credit equivalent to 3 months of expected steady-state spend (will be line-item on the term sheet).
- Committed term: 12 months post-pilot with quarterly usage true-ups allowed in year 1 (we'll reconcile overages at the same committed rates).
- SLA during pilot: 99.5% p99 latency target with a financial credit schedule (outlined in attached term sheet).
- Legal: data residency carveouts noted; we'll surface controlled language and a redline-ready clause for your counsel.

Technical contact for migration week: laura_bennett@redwood.com (she will be on-call and coordinate runbook execution).

Next steps:
1) I will upload the MAP to the HubSpot record and share the DocuSign link for the non-binding pilot terms.
2) If procurement signs off, we target pilot kickoff Jun 21.

Deliverables attached: proposed-term-sheet-helixdata.pdf, redwood-pilot-runbook.pdf

Look forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
[Attachments: proposed-term-sheet-helixdata.pdf, redwood-pilot-runbook.pdf]
